articles.title: The Early History of Smalltalk
articles.summary: The early history of Smalltalk was shaped by the ideas of the 1960s, particularly in the ARPA community, which gave rise to notions of "human-computer symbiosis" through interactive time-shared computers and graphics screens. Advanced computer languages were developed to simulate complex systems, and the work of the sixties was seen as something more than a "better old thing" to be adopted in modern personal computing. articles.title: Async Rust: Where does the scheduler live?
articles.summary: The original idea of this article was to explore the location of the scheduler in async Rust, which is a common complaint among developers. The concept of the scheduler is central to the async runtime, and its implementation is a key aspect of the language. The article delves into the details of the scheduler, including its role in managing concurrency, parallelism, and borrowing, and how it differs from the traditional scoped threads API. This discussion is essential for developers working with async Rust, as it provides insight into the language's design and its implications for performance and scalability.
